Definition: Everything in one part of a game, such as a level or a room: its items, lights, sounds and cameras, and where each one is.
A tool for building a scene by placing and changing items directly, instead of writing code for each one.
One thing in a scene, such as a cube, a tree, a light or a sound.
A file a game uses, such as a picture, a 3D model or a sound.
Usable by people with disabilities, for example with a screen reader, with only a keyboard, or with only a mouse.
A number that gives a position along one direction. A position in 2D needs two coordinates, x and y; a position in 3D needs three, x, y and z.
The direction that runs left and right. Larger x values are farther to the right.
The direction that runs up and down. Larger y values are higher.
In 3D, the direction that runs toward and away from you. In Quorum, larger z values are farther away.
The point where every coordinate is 0: (0, 0) in 2D or (0, 0, 0) in 3D. Every other position is measured from it.
